It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 16, 2020}} The district consists of the provincial capital, [[Tacloban]], and adjacent municipalities of [[Alangalang, Leyte|Alangalang]], [[Babatngon]], [[Palo, Leyte|Palo]], [[San Miguel, Leyte|San Miguel]], [[Santa Fe, Leyte|Santa Fe]], [[Tanauan, Leyte|Tanauan]] and [[Tolosa, Leyte|Tolosa]] since 1987. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Martin Romualdez]] of the [[Lakas–CMD]] (Lakas), who served as the [[Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines|House Speaker]] from July 2022 to September 2025.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 16, 2020}} Until 1931, it consisted of the sub-province of [[Biliran]] and the northwestern municipalities of [[Albuera, Leyte|Albuera]], [[Baybay]], [[Calubian]], [[Leyte, Leyte|Leyte]], [[Merida, Leyte|Merida]], [[Ormoc]], [[Palompon]], [[San Isidro, Leyte|San Isidro]], and [[Villaba]]. Following the creation of the [[Leyte's 5th congressional district|fifth district]], Albuera, Baybay, and Ormoc were redistricted to the [[Leyte's 2nd congressional district|second district]], while other municipalities were retained;{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=3788|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5564 |title=An Act Reorganizing the Representative Districts of the Province of Leyte and Creating a Fifth District|date=December 2, 1930 |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate= May 6, 2020}} [[Isabel, Leyte|Isabel]], [[Matag-ob]], and [[Tabango]] were later established as new municipalities after the district was re-created in 1945. Following the creation of [[Southern Leyte]] in 1959, these areas under this district were reapportioned to the [[Leyte's 3rd congressional district|third district]], and the district was redefined to consist of the city of Tacloban and the eastern municipalities of [[Abuyog]], Babatngon, [[Dulag, Leyte|Dulag]], [[Javier, Leyte|Javier]], [[MacArthur, Leyte|MacArthur]], [[Mahaplag]], [[Mayorga, Leyte|Mayorga]], Palo, San Miguel, Santa Fe, Tanauan, and Tolosa, all previously from the [[Leyte's 4th congressional district|fourth district]], from 1961 until its second dissolution in 1972.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=2227|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html |title=An Act Creating the Province of Southern Leyte|date=May 22, 1959 |publisher=The Lawphil Project - Arellano Law Foundation, Inc. |accessdate=6 May 2020}} Together with [[Negros Occidental's 3rd congressional district|Negros Occidental's 3rd district]], Leyte's 1st district has seen two House Speakers, tied for the most by any district: [[Daniel Z.
